title: Account Page Count
prompt: A TypeScript list view paginates accounts. Write a function that returns how many pages are needed for a total item count and page size.

explanation.beginner:
Example: accountPageCount(21, 10) produces 3. Divide the item count by page size and round upward so a partial final page still counts.

Compare “handles exact pages”: input [20,10] produces 2. Explain which rule causes the difference before writing code.
explanation.junior:
Divide the item count by page size and round upward so a partial final page still counts.

Tempting mistake: Truncation or ordinary rounding loses a partially filled page; zero items and exact multiples are useful boundaries.

Trace the branch conditions and any accumulator or lookup after each input. Keep the return contract separate from how it is calculated.

Regression check: preserve the contract illustrated by “handles exact pages”, then change one boundary in a new test. The solution below is one implementation; another is valid when it preserves the same behavior.
